PC: C, A, Bs should be quickly assessed
Place patient on full cardiac monitor
Obtain labs including venous blood gas, CBC, blood culture
Trial bronchodilator therapy and consider IM Epinephrine
Consider broad-spectrum antibiotics such as ceftriaxone
MK: Recognize vital sign abnormalities of tachypnea, hypoxia and tachycardia
Identify potential need for advanced respiratory support and potential difficult airway
Learners verbalize their interpretation of labs, CXR and EKG
SBP: Identify patient as a Person Under Investigation (PUI) and don appropriate PPE
Limit personnel in the room when treating with aerosolizing treatments or procedures
If necessary, move patient to a negative pressure room or room with a HEPA filter
Call for respiratory therapy and consider calling PICU or anesthesia for support
ICS: Verbalize infection exposure concerns to prompt healthcare team members to also don appropriate PPE
Effectively communicate concerns for respiratory failure with healthcare team
